author: root_pi
question: Do the deposited records support a small whole-microcosm predictive test of predator and parasite effects?
hypothesis: The source map can either qualify a bounded treatment-response reanalysis or show a specific measurement or coverage failure before fitting.

sources.note: Official metadata inspected; two selected count/exposure CSVs identified. No source rows acquired in the restart screen.
Published conclusions and parameter table were exposed during search. They are prior work, never priors or desired answers.

measurement: Metadata-only map from two specified files. Numeric count and Colonies fields stay opaque and unconverted. Unit, exposure and sampling facts that remain unknown block fit readiness.
independent_unit: Candidate unit is a microcosm repID; biological independence and cross-file joins remain to be established. Species/day rows are not independent cultures.
models: smaller net treatment-interaction model if mechanism identification is not justified
baseline: No fitting at this stage. A later plan needs the smallest useful treatment or dynamic baseline, independent of published estimates.
reference: Official source identity, full treatment and per-unit coverage map are the reference for this gate. A later likelihood/reference design requires separate review.
split: No outcomes or final split selected. Preserve whole microcosms; never use published exclusions or outcome values for selection.
cheap_test: Map every prey/predator/parasite combination and repID. Require all four prey-present candidate arms, at least two documented units per arm, and three PARA days per candidate unit; predator-present units also need three DIDI days. Keep all failures visible.
risks: Units and sample removal or replacement may remain unknown.
Metadata minima do not establish power, independence or parameter identification.
Published results are exposed; any later test is a reanalysis.
A source-stage GO does not authorize counts, fitting or held-out scoring.
